Meta.title: Taksu Tech: robotics built by young Balinese engineers
Meta.description: Taksu Tech, part of Ezra Robotics: Bali receptionist robots (Snow, Timo, and Taksu Kiosk) and education robot kits for primary to senior high, with a simulator and a full curriculum.

hero.title: Robotics built by young Balinese engineers
hero.body: We design receptionist robots that understand Balinese custom and education robot kits for schools across Indonesia. Taksu Tech is part of Ezra Robotics.
hero.imageAlt: Snow and Timo Bali Edition robots in traditional dress in a hotel lobby
hero.caption: Snow and Timo Bali Edition, modified by Taksu Tech

divisions.title: Two product lines
divisions.intro: One team in Bali that designs, installs, teaches, and maintains the robots.
divisions.educationImageAlt: Education robots for primary, junior, and senior high on a classroom desk

aksara.title: Follows the Aksara Bali regulation
aksara.body: Screens and printouts show Aksara Bali above Latin, following Bali Governor Regulation 80/2018.

kiosk.title: A kiosk built in Bali
kiosk.body: Taksu Kiosk is assembled in Bali with high local content and a built-in printer.

kka.title: Aligned with the KKA subject
kka.body: The education curriculum maps to the elective Coding and Artificial Intelligence subject.

simulator.title: Free to try in the browser
simulator.body: The robot simulator and kiosk demos work without signing in.

demos.title: Try it in your browser
demos.intro: Talk to a receptionist robot, print a visitor pass, or program a robot in the simulator.
demos.launcher: Pick your own robot and sample venue

values.title: Tri Hita Karana in how we work
values.intro: Three sources of harmony in Balinese philosophy, and what they mean for our products.

cta.title: Want to see the robots in person?
cta.body: We can visit your office, hotel, or school for a demo.

Reception.metaTitle: Bali receptionist robots: Snow, Timo, and Taksu Kiosk
Reception.metaDescription: Bali Edition receptionist robots and a Bali-built kiosk that support Aksara Bali per Regulation 80/2018, print tickets and visitor passes, and hold a spoken conversation.

hero.title: Receptionist robots that greet with Om Swastiastu
hero.body: Snow and Timo Bali Edition in traditional dress, plus our own Taksu Kiosk. All of them show Aksara Bali, print tickets and visitor passes, and talk with guests in Indonesian or English.
hero.imageAlt: Snow and Timo Bali Edition in Balinese traditional dress

robots.title: Choose your receptionist
robots.intro: Two mobile robots we modify for Bali, and one static kiosk we build ourselves.

features.title: One kiosk app for all three
features.intro: We build the Taksu kiosk software ourselves, so it adapts to your services.

voice.title: Holds a conversation
voice.body: Speech recognition and the robot’s voice run on your own server, not an outside service. Guests just ask; the robot answers from your venue’s data.

bali.title: Knows the Balinese calendar
bali.intro: The robot’s greetings and notices follow the holy days of the Pawukon calendar.
bali.nextHoly: {name} in {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}

aksara.metaTitle: Aksara Bali on robots and kiosks
aksara.metaDescription: Digital signage and printouts with Aksara Bali above Latin, following Bali Governor Regulation 80/2018 and Bali Regional Regulation 1/2018.
aksara.title: Aksara Bali on every screen and printout
aksara.intro: Our kiosks write venue names in Aksara Bali above the Latin script, following Bali’s signage rules.

useCases.title: Where our robots work
useCases.intro: Every venue moves guests differently. We tailor the content and the robot.

process.title: How we install
process.intro: From the site survey to a robot at work in your lobby.

compare.metaTitle: Compare Snow, Timo, and Taksu Kiosk
compare.metaDescription: Snow and Timo Bali Edition compared with the Bali-built Taksu Kiosk: mobility, printing, local content, and price.
compare.title: Compare all three
compare.intro: Mobile robots for a lively experience, a static kiosk for affordable printing and high local content.
compare.note: The Taksu Kiosk TKDN percentage follows official certification.

Edu.metaTitle: Taksu Edu: education robots for primary to senior high
Edu.metaDescription: Customisable education robot kits, a free simulator, a 32–36 meeting curriculum, and teacher guides. Aligned with the Coding and AI subject.

hero.title: Learn robotics from simulation to a real robot
hero.body: Customisable robot kits for primary, junior, and senior high, with a free simulator, a meeting-by-meeting curriculum, and teacher guides.
hero.imageAlt: Poster of the learning flow from simulation to a real robot

advantages.title: Why schools choose Taksu Edu
advantages.intro: We do not just sell kits. We prepare how to teach with them.

levels.title: One path from primary to senior high
levels.intro: Robots, modules, and lessons connect across levels.
levels.imageAlt: Education robots for primary, junior, and senior high

path.title: The flow of every meeting
path.intro: Students try in the simulator first, then run it on the real robot.

upgrade.title: Upgrade path
upgrade.intro: Every platform is compatible and upgradeable at any time.

support.title: After-sales and support
support.intro: We stay with schools after the purchase.

competitions.title: Competition ready
competitions.body: Advanced material is prepared for the {list} tracks.

curriculum.metaDescription: A 32-meeting primary robotics syllabus and 36-meeting junior and senior high syllabi, with goals, evidence of learning, rubrics, and KKA mapping.
curriculum.title: Curriculum and syllabus
curriculum.intro: Every level has modules, a per-meeting plan, evidence of learning, and an assessment rubric.
curriculum.kkaIntro: The Coding and Artificial Intelligence elements this level strengthens most.
curriculum.tiersIntro: Variations of activity on the same robot, not three different devices.
curriculum.rubricIntro: Assess the process, not only whether the first program worked.

guides.metaDescription: Guides to start the robot, run a class, assemble the junior high robot, stay safe with batteries, and use the simulator.
guides.title: Guides
guides.intro: Practical steps for teachers, students, and schools.

simulator.metaDescription: Try primary and junior high robot missions in the browser: motion, line sensors, distance, servo radar, temperature, and sound, with a C++ preview.
simulator.title: A free simulation platform
simulator.intro: Schools can try every mission before buying a robot. The simulator mimics the real robot’s sensors and outputs.

features.physics: Left and right wheel motion, speed, and turning
features.distance: Ultrasonic distance, including on a servo
features.outputs: OLED face, OLED text, and buzzer
features.env: Temperature, humidity, and claps for junior high
features.code: A C++ preview of the blocks you build

simulator.trialBody: Want the simulator in your computer lab with custom missions? We set up access and a short training.

custom.metaDescription: Robot kits and curricula tailored for schools, campuses, research, industry, and special projects.
custom.title: Custom to your needs

custom.pcbAlt: Custom PCB for the modular robot
custom.pcbCaption: Our custom PCB: where sensors, driver, power, and the ESP32 come together.
